newsitem.title: CANADA: Ex-Canada rates firm undertone but rangebound.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Canada rates firm undertone but rangebound.

text.p: While Canadian international rates remain little changed from the summer, carriers and forwarders said a definite firming trend is under way in major export corridors that goes beyond the usual seasonal buildup and may be the beginning of a full blown recovery.
The recovery is evident in ex-Canada rates to Hong Kong, where strong demand has permitted Air Canada, Canadian Airlines Corp and others to increase rates by 10-15 percent since mid-September.
"This increase just about gets us back to where things were last March," said an official of one carrier, making reference to the broad decline in most ex-Canada rates last spring.

As a measure of the buoyancy of Pacific routes, Vancouver airport reported import freight traffic in August soared 29.2 percent to 6,296 tonnes over the year-ago level and exports shot up 16.2 percent to 8,443 tonnes.
These increases far exceeded the airport's cargo traffic in the preceding seven months, when export freight was up just 5.7 percent.
On the North Atlantic, evidence of a recovery is anecdotal.
North Atlantic rates remains substantially unchanged from the summer, but yields - the net per-kg revenues of the carriers - are said to be firming for three reasons.
First, September and October traffic has been particularly strong - better than for the same months a year ago and approaching the boom levels of 1994.
Also, the withdrawal of seasonal charters, coupled with major restructuring of the competitive alignment on some key corridors, are helping put an end to discounting.
On some routes yields have recovered to, and are beginning to exceed, year-ago levels, airline sources said.

In general, ex-Canada rates to Europe remain rangebound, reflecting the reputation and capabilities of competing carriers. European carriers with large global cargo networks and main-deck freighter or combi capacity tend to have substantially higher fixed costs, and price at the top of the range. Others
